App Store

Anamorphic Desqueezer — live monitor & CinemaScope

Live monitor: real-time de-squeeze, squeezed / desqueezed toggle, 2.39:1 guides, true anamorphic aspect. Scopes: zebras, IRE waveform, false color, peaking, luma/RGB histogram, ISO / shutter / WB. Export: true 2.39:1 CinemaScope — no stretched footage — ProRes / 10-bit to Photos or Files, FCPXML for Final Cut, per-clip framing, LUT, trim. Photo & batch: DNG stills, batch clips, per-clip or merged timeline.

iOS + MacBook overview

  • Live monitor + post: 1.33×–2× and custom ratio
  • ProRes & 10-bit, FCPXML, 2.39:1 export
  • Zebras, waveform, false color for exposure
  • Batch-friendly workflow for set and editorial handoff

Why crews keep it on the phone

  • Live desqueeze preview matches what you will deliver.
  • ProRes and 10-bit HEVC when iOS allows — not just a proxy.
  • Zebras, false color, and peaking for exposure and focus.
  • Batch passes and DNG stills when the day calls for coverage.

iPhone & iPad specifics

  • iPad storyboard lane? Use Split View: keep script sheets open while the live preview runs full width on the other half.
  • External monitor? Mirror the corrected signal when directors want to sign off without hovering over the operator.
  • Battery shoots? Pre-build ratio presets per lens serial so you are not menu-diving between setups.
  • FCPXML round-trip? Export after each location wrap so editorial inherits reel names before proxies get renamed on the shuttle drive.

Handoff

Post picks up your intent.

Feed ARRI, RED, Blackmagic, or Panasonic over SDI/HDMI, grade live with scopes, and record graded ProRes — so dailies match what editorial will relink, not a guess.

Buy on Mac App Store Watch on YouTube
Full specs & workflow notes

Post handoff

Packages CDL, AMF, LUT, and EDL+CDL so Resolve, Silverstack, and editorial can re-link the same look. Stills and per-scene looks stay in the library across setups.

Who it's for

Cinematographers, DITs, and colorists who need the final look while the camera is rolling — indies through full crews.

  • Live grading — 3D LUTs and CDL-style primaries, 2.39:1 support, waveform, parade, histogram, vectorscope.
  • Recording — graded ProRes with optional burn-in (timecode, reel/scene/take, slate).
  • Dailies — graded ProRes plus CDL/AMF/LUT and EDL+CDL packages.
  • Shot library — stills and looks per scene; import/export CDL and LUT.

You see what the camera sees, with your look applied. What you record is what the editor expects — predictable from set to dailies.
